jobs.title: Senior Product Manager
jobs.description:
About Bobyard
Construction is a multi-trillion-dollar industry that still estimates by hand. Contractors measure and count materials off drawings manually, and it caps how many jobs they can bid. Bobyard uses computer vision and NLP to automate takeoffs and estimates, so contractors bid faster and win more. We raised a $35M Series A led by 8VC, with Primary and Pear, and we're growing fast.

About the role
As we scale the core product and launch new 0→1 bets, you'll own a roadmap end to end. You'll spend real time with estimators, PMs, and GCs, decide what we build and cut, and ship it with engineering and design.

What you'll do
• Spend real time with customers until you know their workflow cold
• Shape the roadmap: what we build, what we cut, and why
• Take 0→1 ideas from concept to shipped, tested, and iterated
• Work side by side with engineering and design, no handoffs
• Align with marketing and sales on how we position what we ship

What we're looking for
• 5+ years in product management in B2B SaaS
• Shipped 0→1 products with real customer traction
• You turn heavy customer input into a clear plan
• High ownership and comfort with ambiguity
• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or the equivalent combination of education and specialized experience

Nice to have
• AI/ML product experience
• Construction or workflow-heavy software

A note on pace
We move fast, and priorities shift as we learn from customers. Playbooks, context, and requirements are often incomplete when work starts, and you'll be expected to shape them. If that pace excites you, you'll fit in well.

What we offer
Cash for stability. Bonus for performance. Equity for ownership. Your package reflects your role, your experience, and what you deliver, and it grows as you do.
• $150,000–$170,000 base + bonus + 0.02%–0.05% equity
• Medical, dental, and vision coverage
• 401(k) with a 100% match up to 4%
• Catered lunch in the office and $70 a month toward your commute
• Full-time, in person at our San Francisco office (101 2nd Street), 4 days a week.

On sponsorship
We sponsor work visas for this role.

 
 





Comp Philosophy 

Cash for stability. Bonus for performance. Equity for ownership. Your package reflects your role, your experience, and what you deliver.

jobs.title: Technical Product Manager
jobs.description:
About Bobyard
 Construction is a multi-trillion industry running on PDFs, rulers, and 1990s software. The biggest choke point is the cost estimate. Takeoffs are manual, slow, and one mistake blows millions. We use computer vision and NLP to read drawings like an expert estimator, 10x faster and with fewer mistakes. We're backed by 8VC, Primary, and Pear.

About the role
 You'll own a model-powered product surface end to end: not writing specs and handing them off, but being the person engineering and customers both come to when the question is "why did the model do that, and what do we do about it."

What you'll do

 - Own the roadmap for a model-powered product surface, from customer problem to shipped feature

 - Read eval reports and confusion matrices well enough to argue with the CV engineers, not just relay their conclusions

 - Make and defend accuracy/speed/cost tradeoffs — in the room with engineering, and directly with customers

 - Build and maintain eval sets that keep the team honest about model performance

 - Decide when a model is actually ready to ship — not based on aggregate accuracy, but on which failure modes are cheap to catch downstream and which are expensive to miss

 - Turn ambiguous customer complaints ("it missed something") into a specific, testable model or UX fix

 - Work daily with our CV and ML engineers as a peer who understands the model, not a translator layer

What we're looking for

 - 4+ years in product, with real ownership of a model-powered feature (not just "worked with" a data science team)

 - Fluent in model evaluation — precision, recall, false positive/negative tradeoffs — and can reason about when "85% accurate" is good enough versus when it isn't, based on the cost of the specific errors, not just the aggregate number

 - Has shipped 0-to-1 or a major iteration on an ML/CV-driven product in B2B SaaS

 - Comfortable being the last line of defense on "will this model actually work" for customers and execs

 - Fast learner — no construction background required, but you'll need to be dangerous in it within 30 days

 - Ships fast, iterates in public, doesn't hide behind process

Nice to have

 - Prior experience specifically in computer vision (vs. NLP/LLM-only)

 - Background at a company like Scale AI, Labelbox, Samsara, Matterport, Cape Analytics, or DroneDeploy

 - Comfortable in Figma and reading code, even if you don't ship it

What we offer

 - $160K–$180K base + equity

 - Full-time, in-person in San Francisco — we build together
   


Comp Philosophy 

Cash for stability. Bonus for performance. Equity for ownership. Your package reflects your role, your experience, and what you deliver.

jobs.title: Product Operations Manager
jobs.description:
About Bobyard
Construction is a trillion dollar industry running on manual work. Contractors still measure and count materials off drawings by hand — it takes forever. Bobyard uses AI to automate takeoffs and estimates, making bids 10x faster. We're Series A, backed by 8VC, Primary, and Pear, and we're shipping faster than most teams can track.



About the role 
The product team is launching new trades, features, and fixes constantly — sometimes a dozen projects in flight at once. Right now, nobody owns making sure what ships is actually fixed, actually launched, and actually communicated. That's this role. You'll sit between engineering and every customer-facing team, verify that bugs are really resolved before we tell anyone they're fixed, and make sure every launch comes with a clear, honest update to the people who need it — customers, CSMs, and sales alike.



What you'll do

 - Own the day-to-day truth of Linear — every ticket has a real status, nothing goes stale or slips silently past its target date

 - Independently verify that "fixed" tickets are actually fixed before they're closed or communicated

 - Write and send launch communications for every release — clear, specific, no corporate filler — to customers and internal teams

 - Build and run a standard launch checklist so marketing and CS are looped in before a release, not briefed after

 - Coordinate directly with Platform engineers on active projects — you're in their tickets, not waiting on a summary

 - Flag risk and slippage early, in the same weekly rhythm the product team already runs

 - Be the first call when a customer says something's broken and an engineer says it isn't



What we're looking for

 - 2–5 years in a role that combined technical coordination with customer-facing communication — Implementation, CS Ops, QA, or release coordination

 - Fluent in Linear or Jira — daily use, not passing familiarity

 - Can write the same update two ways: technical for engineers, plain for customers

 - Comfortable pushing back on an engineer's "it's fixed" claim without making it a fight

 - Genuinely enjoys verification and follow-through — you don't lose interest once something's "probably done"

 - Based in or willing to relocate to San Francisco



Nice to have



 - Experience at a Series A–C startup with no dedicated QA team

 - Background in construction tech, PropTech, or a technical B2B product

 - Experience building a launch or release process from scratch



What we offer $120,000–$150,000 base, 0.02%–0.04% equity (4-year vest, 1-year cliff), on-site in San Francisco.



Comp Philosophy 

Cash for stability. Bonus for performance. Equity for ownership. Your package reflects your role, your experience, and what you deliver.
